title: Jeus: ask your data a question
reference: Modelled on bioglyph/video/script.json: 7 segments, under two minutes, 13-16 s each, two or three declarative sentences per segment, no filler. Every number is from the manuscript's released records (jeus/assets/results.js and examples.js); scenes.py reads them from those files so the picture and the voice cannot drift apart.
voice_notes: Numbers are written the way the neural voice reads them correctly. Percentages spelled as 'percent'. 'FOXL1 positive' rather than 'FOXL1+'. Model names as spoken: 'GLM five point three'. Each segment's `caption` is the written form of the same sentences (digits, symbols, the URL) and goes into the WebVTT track; `narration` is what is spoken.

segments.narration: A folder of biomedical data, and a question. Which genes separate the two patient groups? Answering it means loading the files, choosing a method, writing the code, running it, and reading what comes back.
segments.visual: Left: a folder card whose file list types in, in mono. Right: the question in serif with a blinking cursor. Lower: the five verbs appear one by one.
segments.caption: A folder of biomedical data, and a question. Which genes separate the two patient groups? Answering it means loading the files, choosing a method, writing the code, running it, and reading what comes back.

segments.narration: Jeus is an AI agent that does this with a language model, open-weight or proprietary. It writes and runs analysis code one step at a time, and every step is recorded.
segments.visual: A vertical timeline of steps with ticks landing one after another: list the files, write the analysis, run it, read the result, go on to the next step, write the answer. Right: a log card that fills line by line.
segments.caption: Jeus is an AI agent that does this with a language model, open-weight or proprietary. It writes and runs analysis code one step at a time, and every step is recorded.

segments.narration: Take a question from BAISBench, a benchmark built on published single-cell studies. What role did FOXL1 positive fibroblasts play in intestinal development? Four options, and the answer key says A.
segments.visual: The published question as a card: the stem in serif, the four options A to D in sans with mono letters, then 'answer key: A' in accent.
segments.caption: Take a question from BAISBench, a benchmark built on published single-cell studies. What role did FOXL1+ fibroblasts play in intestinal development? Four options, and the answer key says A.

segments.narration: With GLM five point three, Jeus read the single-cell data, tabulated candidate genes across the fetal cell clusters, and answered A in twenty-one model calls. The same model in Codex CLI answered A and D; in Claude Code, A.
segments.visual: Three outcome cards side by side, Jeus first with an accent border: the answer letters large, correct or incorrect, calls and tokens. Under Jeus's card, its recorded method summary from the manuscript.
segments.caption: With GLM-5.3, Jeus read the single-cell data, tabulated candidate genes across the fetal cell clusters, and answered A in 21 model calls. The same model in Codex CLI answered A and D; in Claude Code, A.

segments.narration: Across five open-weight models and three benchmarks, Jeus had the highest five-model mean: fifty-one point three percent on BixBench, eighty-four point four on Verified-50, and sixty-eight point zero on BAISBench.
segments.visual: Grouped bars growing from a shared axis for BixBench, Verified-50 and BAISBench: Jeus in accent, Codex CLI blue, Claude Code green, Biomni A1 plum where evaluated, each labelled with its value.
segments.caption: Across five open-weight models and three benchmarks, Jeus had the highest five-model mean: 51.3% on BixBench, 84.4% on Verified-50, and 68.0% on BAISBench.

segments.narration: The other agents used four point one to twenty-four point four times the peak process memory of Jeus. With Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Sol, Jeus's model-access costs were twenty-four to eighty-one percent lower in fourteen of sixteen comparisons.
segments.visual: Two stat cards fading in: '4.1–24.4×' with 'peak process memory of Codex CLI, Claude Code and Biomni A1, relative to Jeus, 28 benchmark summaries', and '24–81% lower' with 'model-access costs, 14 of 16 comparisons'. The numbers are shown as they are, never counted up, so a paused frame never shows a wrong value.
segments.caption: The other agents used 4.1 to 24.4 times the peak process memory of Jeus. With Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Sol, Jeus's model-access costs were 24 to 81 percent lower in 14 of 16 comparisons.

segments.narration: The manuscript also evaluates twenty-four clinical prediction tasks with the same agents and models. Every number here comes from its released records. Islam lab dot org, slash jeus.
segments.visual: Closing card: the Jeus wordmark, 'islamlab.org/jeus', and a caps line: five benchmarks, 24 clinical prediction tasks, open-weight or proprietary models.
segments.caption: The manuscript also evaluates 24 clinical prediction tasks with the same agents and models. Every number here comes from its released records. islamlab.org/jeus
